title: Guided Notes

vocab.Bias: A study is biased when its procedure systematically misses the population value the same way every time --- a direction, not bad luck.
vocab.Sampling bias: Bias from how the sample was chosen: some members of the population are more likely to be picked than others.
vocab.Undercoverage: Part of the population is left off the sampling frame, so those members have no chance at all of being chosen.
vocab.Nonresponse: Members are chosen properly but never answer, so the data is missing exactly the people who stayed silent.
vocab.Response bias: Anything about the survey itself --- who asks, the wording, the order --- that pushes a respondent off their true answer.
